newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Worries wobble Brussels bourse, future unclear.
newsitem.headline: Worries wobble Brussels bourse, future unclear.

text.p: Nervous profit-taking on worries about the formation of the new French government met still strong underlying sentiment to leave the Brussels bourse off a new intra-day high but still at a new closing high on Wednesday.
"People are quite worried about what will happen in France tonight, so some of them took the chance to take profits," one trader said.

"It depends how the communists are placed in the government. (Prime Minister Lionel) Jospin is not stupid, but people will still be watching carefully. It could have an effect on policy and therefore on the euro," he added.
Traders said that if the doubts about the ability of the European Union to stick to its single currency schedule grew then interest rates would rise and stocks would suffer.
If, on the other hand, the worries receded then the sky would once again be the limit for the bourse as fundamentals remained sound.
Much of the uncertainty should be settled one way or the other at the EU's summit in Amsterdam on June 16 and 17, but the intervening period could become fairly volatile, traders said.
The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares ended a moderately busy Wednesday up 0.16 percent to a new closing high of 2,284.40.
It had earlier hit a new intra-day high of 2,290.16. A total of some 3.3 billion francs of Belgian shares changed hands.

Non-ferrous metals group Union Miniere was one of the main gainers of the day, rising 2.5 percent to 3,040 francs on a hefty turnover of nearly 63,000 shares, boosted by the strong dollar and one big buyer.
Insurer Royale Belge was also busy, falling 0.5 percent to 10,100 francs on profit-taking.
Oil major PetroFina was also active, dropping 1.2 percent to 12,300 francs -- well off the 12,500 francs exercise price of a share buying warrant that expired on Tuesdsay.
Traders had mixed views on whether the warrant issue, designed to raise capital for the firm, had been a success or not.
Some said the fee structure for institutions had been such that they expected many of the warrants to have been exercised, while others said it had been an embarrassing flop.
PetroFina is expected to make an announcement on Thursday.
The other major feature of the market on Wednesday was news of the possible merger between power utility Electrabel and holding company Tractebel. Analysts welcomed it as broadly good for both firms.
The merger would be the biggest in Belgian bourse history and create a company worth about one-seventh of the Brussels bourse capitalisation.
Tractebel shares ended 0.32 percent lower at 15,525 francs, while Electrabel closed 0.64 percent lower at 7,790 francs.

"Electrabel shares have always been held by Belgian citizens rather like bonds, always paying a nice steady dividend. Holding shares in a big industrial concern like Tractebel would not be the same," one trader said. "So there are some worries there."
